Subject: Initial questions on SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist windows and service accounts

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the product overview last week — team appreciated the walkthrough. We're getting our infra team aligned and have a few immediate questions as we draft our internal cutover plan:

- For SSO (SAML), can you confirm whether Redwood requires any specific NameID format or can we use email as the persistent identifier?
- SCIM: Do you support incremental syncs and are there rate limits we should design for?
- IP allowlists: we operate with a locked-down edge and will only open outbound whitelists for short maintenance windows. What is the minimum advance notice Redwood needs to schedule a production cutover window so we can align security approvals?
- Service accounts: we have agents that need to call the API (audit scanning, reporting). Is there guidance on ephemeral service accounts vs. long-lived keys for these workflows?

Would you be able to share a mutual action plan and a checklist we can present to our security approvers? Also cc'ing our IT alias so they have context.

Thanks,

Alice Park
Director, IT Operations
Cedar Bank

Subject: Re: Initial questions on SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist windows and service accounts

Hi Alice — great to hear from you and glad the walkthrough was helpful. Short answers up front then I9ll loop in our CS/implementation leads for sequencing and a concrete MAP.

- NameID: email is fine as the persistent NameID. We support email and transient formats; if you prefer a non-email NameID we'll need to map it in SCIM during provisioning.
- SCIM: we support incremental delta syncs (changedUsers/changedGroups). Recommended sync cadence for large orgs is every 5 minutes; our practical rate limit for delta calls is documented but we can increase the cadence for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- IP allowlists: for the hosted API we run scheduled deployment windows and prefer 48-72 hours notice for policy approvals. For reserved/dedicated customers we can accommodate shorter windows (24 hours) if we lock to a fixed egress range — we can provide the IP block list to submit to your security team.
- Service accounts: we recommend using short-lived tokens (via your KMS or a short TTL) for internal agents and ephemeral keys when possible. For integrations that require non-interactive access we support scoped service accounts with fine-grained permissions.

I attached a compact checklist (id-bootstrap-checklist.xlsx) and a template MAP (cedarbank-mutual-action-plan.pdf) to get started.

I'll forward this to Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (implementation PM) to propose dates and runbook items. Can we target the week of Mar 20 for a dry-run in staging?

Best,

Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
